# ui::WindowPlacement

Header: `winui/ui/WindowShell.hpp`.

Where a window was, in a form an app can store on close and hand back on the next run ([Window::placement()](window.md#placement), [ui::WindowOptions::placement](window-options.md)). The app decides where to store it, such as in a file or the registry. A saved monitor that has since gone away is not a problem, since the OS pulls the window back on screen when the placement is applied.

Example: 
```cpp
// The app's own storage, such as a settings file:
std::optional<ui::WindowPlacement> load_placement();
void                               save_placement(const ui::WindowPlacement& placement);

const std::optional<ui::WindowPlacement> saved = load_placement(); // nullopt on the first run
ui::Window editor{{.title = "Editor", .placement = saved}};
ui::run(editor);
if (auto p = editor.placement()) save_placement(*p); // where the window was when it closed
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `normal_bounds` | `Rect` |  | The restored bounds, in DIPs, screen coordinates. They are kept while the window is minimized, maximized or full screen. |
| `state` | `WindowState` | `WindowState::Normal` | The state the window was in when the placement was read; the next run shows in it. |
| `restore_to_maximized` | `bool` | `false` | Whether leaving Minimized or Fullscreen goes back to Maximized rather than Normal. |
